acceptance_signals: STATUS.md retains the current closeout snapshot and current capability reality while clearly superseded dated checkpoint sections are replaced by concise links to preserved historical evidence.
DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md retains strategic direction and priority sequencing while clearly current-state and completed-session history blocks are moved out of the strategy surface.
docs/development-plan.md retains public strategic ordering while old current-checkpoint and next-session evidence is moved out of the public strategy surface.
A dated migration log preserves relocated historical facts, original section identity, and repository-relative evidence references without rewriting past outcomes.
Documentation tests protect canonical ownership, preserved history links, and the absence of the migrated historical headings from current-state and strategy surfaces.
Focused documentation and task-contract tests pass, the baseline unittest suite passes, and git diff --check reports no whitespace errors.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-14 Historical Documentation Migration v1 relocated four exact section-bounded history blocks into one source-labeled dated record while current status and strategic plans retained concise ownership pointers. Exact text comparison passed after documented heading demotion; 46 focused documentation/task tests, the Harness cross-document regression, and the complete 810-test suite passed with 2 skips. Repository governance had no failure, and a distinct native current-Agent self-review found no requirement, scope, architecture, implementation, data, or authority drift requiring correction. This paused task authorizes no broader cleanup, archive automation, Git action, publication, release, deployment, or follow-on implementation.

requirement.summary: Implement Historical Documentation Migration v1 by relocating clearly superseded checkpoint and completed-session history from current status and strategic planning surfaces into a dated, source-labeled development-log record; replace migrated blocks with concise canonical pointers, preserve historical facts and evidence references, and leave current capability, strategy, automation, runtime behavior, Git, release, and deployment semantics unchanged.

items: Over-broad section removal could discard current capability or strategic facts.
Moving text could break internal links or evidence references.
A public-plan edit could drift from the internal strategy surface if protecting tests do not cover both.
Historical material must be labeled as migrated and superseded rather than presented as a new event on the migration date.
Reviewed assumption: Only clearly section-bounded historical checkpoint and completed-session blocks will be migrated; mixed sections that still own current capability or strategy facts will remain.
Reviewed assumption: The selected migration can use one additional dated development-log file for the migration record while preserving all existing log paths.
Reviewed assumption: Public documentation changes are limited to the public development plan because product behavior, commands, release identity, and user journeys do not change.
Reviewed assumption: The existing untracked .codex directory is human-owned and remains untouched.
Reviewed unknown: The final line count reduction is unknown until section-boundary and link validation is complete.

title: Migrate historical documentation checkpoints
